chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from al-Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I heard Abdul Malik ibn Ayn ask Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and he did not cease asking until he said, 'So the people are destroyed.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, by Allah, O Ibn Ayn, the people are destroyed all together.' I said, 'The ones in the East and the ones in the West?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Misguidance has conquered them. Yes, by Allah, they were destroyed except for three.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people saved from destruction according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) confirms to Abdul Malik ibn Ayn that the general populace has perished due to widespread deviation, with only three specific individuals remaining as exceptions. This hadith is often cited in Shia scholarship to highlight the rarity of true guidance and the concept of *al-thalatha* (the three), which some interpret as the Prophet, Imam Ali, and Imam Hasan, or as a symbolic reference to the core group of the faithful during times of widespread misguidance.
